Roof Replacement

We strip the old roof completely, put right what we find underneath and fit a new roof with breathable membrane, pressure-treated battens, new tiles and leadwork. A full replacement usually takes 5 to 10 working days.

Stripped Back, Never Covered Over

We fully strip the existing roof, inspect the structure underneath and deal with any defects we find before the new roof goes on. We never cut corners or cover over problems that are already there.

What Goes Into a New Roof

Quality materials from trusted manufacturers: breathable roofing membranes, pressure-treated battens, good roof tiles, leadwork and modern dry ridge, hip and verge systems. Our own directly employed roofers fit them, we photograph the work throughout, and insurance-backed guarantees are available where they apply.

Recent Jobs

Parkdale Road, Leicester LE4, 2025: complete roof replacements on two neighbouring semi-detached houses, done at the same time. Old tiles, battens and felt all off, then new membrane, treated battens, a new tiled roof and all new leadwork.

Acorn Drive, Belper, 2025: the roof tiles and the closed-cell spray foam all removed and the roof timbers cleaned, then new membrane, treated battens and a complete new tiled roof. Signed off by Building Control and passed by HSBC.

Why People Replace a Roof

  • The roof is getting old
  • Tiles are damaged
  • Leaks keep coming back
  • The roofing materials are breaking down

How Long It Takes

A full roof replacement usually takes 5 to 10 working days, depending on the size of the house, how complex the roof is, the weather and how much work is needed.
